item.title: The heat does not curb meat consumption, but it will increase prices
item.description: The heatwave has not prevented an increase in meat consumption, but the drought could reduce supply and drive up prices.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The heatwave did not prevent an increase in meat consumption. - Drought could reduce supply and drive up prices. - The food industry is preparing for increases due to shortages of raw materials and livestock in advance of slaughter.
## Key facts - **What**: Meat consumption in Switzerland. - When: Heat wave. - Where: Switzerland. - Who: Food industry. - Amount: Price increase.
BASEL - Switzerland's heatwave has so far failed to significantly curb meat consumption, but prolonged drought risks reducing supply and driving up prices. Marco Tschanz, CEO of Bell, one of the main players in the Swiss food sector, sounded the alarm.
"If temperatures exceed 29 degrees for an extended period, meat consumption begins to fall: consumers may have less desire to get in front of the barbecue," explains the executive in an interview with the AWP agency. “But we didn't see a massive drop thissummer. Factors such as holidays or vacations have a greater weight. "
According to data from the Federal Office of Agriculture (FOAG), meat consumption in Switzerland increased by 5.6% in 2022 compared to the previous year. Beef was the most consumed, followed by pork and chicken. Beef consumption increased by 10.3% in 2022, while pork consumption increased by 4.5%.

The lack of water is already having repercussions on the entire supply chain. Small-leaf salads are in part almost unobtainable in Europe, so much so that they have been forced to source from Turkey. Even more critical is the situation for livestock: “Due to the drought the animals are brought downstream for slaughter earlier than expected: this means that we will miss thatoffer later in the year.”
According to data from the Federal Office for Agriculture (FOAG), the cost of meat production in Switzerland increased by 10% compared to the same period last year. This is mainly due to the scarcity of animal feed, which increased in price by 15% on average. "The situation is critical especially for the production of beef and pork, which represent the majority of the Swiss market," explains a representative of the food industry.
The situation is even more worrying for the regions most affected by the drought, such as the Canton of Ticino and the Grisons region. According to a monthly survey by the Bloomberg agency, taken from the Cash portal, most experts in the financial sector have postponed expectations for the first increase in the cost of money. A large part of the respondents even believe that the increase will not take place before the beginning of 2028. item.description: The Manpower survey has a net forecast of +19. Interest in AI skills is growing, but SMEs are struggling to invest in digital.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Net employment outlook steady at +19. - Hiring levels at a five-year low. - Growing demand for AI skills and soft skills. - SMEs lagging behind large companies.
## Key facts - **What**: Net employment outlook survey. - When: Latest quarter reported by Manpower. - Where: Switzerland. - Who: Manpower. - Amount: Net outlook +19. - Percentage: 56% of employers willing to pay premiums for AI skills.
Swiss companies are facing a period of marked caution in their recruitment strategies, with hiring intentions at their lowest levels in the last five years. According to the periodic analysis conducted by Manpower, a leading multinational in the human resources sector, the so-called 'net employment outlook' has reached +19. This indicator, calculated as the difference between companies intending to increase staff and those planning a reduction, marks a slight progress of just one point compared to the previous quarter. The Swiss figure is positioned significantly below the global average, highlighting a 7-percentage-point gap.
### Market factors analysis Eric Jeannerod, head of Manpower in Switzerland, emphasized how companies have achieved greater stability in operational planning. However, this security does not translate into aggressive workforce expansion. The persistent climate of caution is directly attributable to the decline in demand recorded in major export markets, which heavily influences employers' strategic choices. Despite the slight increase in hiring intentions, the Swiss labor market remains in a cooling phase. Those seeking employment or intending to change jobs should consider that companies, albeit cautiously, are redefining the requirements necessary for recruitment. Digital transformation and the adoption of new technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, are becoming the main drivers for the selection of qualified personnel. It is essential to monitor available opportunities through specialized portals, constantly checking the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) and the salary prospects offered by the various economic sectors operating nationwide, keeping in mind that hiring dynamics are currently influenced by a generalized caution that limits rapid workforce growth in many industrial and service sectors. The labor market is undergoing a phase of profound transformation where the value of digital skills and so-called 'soft skills' is becoming a decisive factor for remuneration. 56% of the companies surveyed confirmed their willingness to offer a salary supplement for specific skills related to artificial intelligence. This trend is even more pronounced in large enterprises with over 250 employees, where the propensity to invest financially in these abilities rises to 66%. The divergence between large companies and small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs) raises critical questions regarding the competitiveness of the Swiss business landscape. While large, structured organizations are able to integrate AI into their production processes, SMEs seem to face greater difficulties, due both to a different perception of the importance of this technology and to the limited availability of financial resources to allocate to training or the acquisition of specialized talent.
### Implications for workers For those working in Switzerland, the current scenario requires constant updating of one's professional profile. The ability to demonstrate AI skills is no longer just an added value, but an element that can directly influence salary levels. The comparison between the demand for digital skills and the market supply highlights how employers are willing to invest more where they see a direct return in terms of operational efficiency. Those who wish to maximize their career chances should carefully evaluate their position against market requirements, using tools such as the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) to understand how their skills align with sectoral salary averages. It is important to note that, in a context of cautious hiring, companies tend to favor candidates who are already trained or possess high potential for technological adaptation. The ability to combine technical digital skills with human relational abilities is the true strength that allows one to pass the selection process in a market phase where employment growth is limited.

## In Brief - Bank loyalty in Switzerland costs up to 1,000 Swiss francs per year. - Diversifying providers results in a positive balance of 229 Swiss francs. - Pillar 3a is the area with the greatest potential for annual savings.
## Key Facts - **What**: Study on bank fees by Moneyland.ch - When: Published today - Where: Switzerland - Who: Moneyland.ch - Amount: 491 Swiss francs (minimum annual cost at Banca Migros) - Amount: 964 Swiss francs (maximum annual cost at UBS)
The Swiss tendency to keep all financial relationships with a single credit institution is proving to be a less-than-astute economic choice. A recent study published by the online comparator Moneyland.ch has analyzed the overall costs associated with managing a standard package of banking services at nine major Swiss institutions. The investigation considers a typical user profile that uses a private account with a debit card, a savings account, a credit card, international payment services, and a pension solution linked to Pillar 3a.
### Analysis of Cost Results The data emerging from the research highlights a significant disparity between the different banks analyzed. Banca Migros is positioned as the most economical option for those who want to centralize their services, with an estimated annual cost of 491 Swiss francs. On the other hand, institutions such as UBS reach costs of up to 964 Swiss francs for the same user profile. Between the two extremes are the Zurich Cantonal Bank (ZKB) with 597 Swiss francs, Valiant with 607 Swiss francs, PostFinance with 736 Swiss francs, and Raiffeisen with 821 Swiss francs. This analysis clearly shows that the cost of loyalty can have a significant impact on the annual family budget, pushing many consumers to consider a more fragmented management of their financial products. The choice to centralize everything at a single bank, although perceived as more convenient, involves a non-negligible expense that directly affects the cost of living in Switzerland. The search for more advantageous banks becomes a necessity for those who want to optimize their financial resources. Transparency of bank fees is a fundamental element for correct financial planning, especially in a context where active interests and commissions vary significantly from one provider to another, making comparison a necessary step for every account holder. The analysis conducted by Moneyland.ch does not only compare banks as a whole, but suggests a diversification strategy that can turn a fixed cost into a potential gain. Dividing products among different specialized suppliers allows selecting the most economical option for each single category on the market.
